about.title: Loyalton Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Loyalton's workforce spans ranching, timber-adjacent trades, small retail along Church Street and Courthouse Square, and public services tied to the county seat. When a task goes wrong — a fall from a ladder, a piece of equipment that malfunctions, a slick loading dock near Beckwith Road — the injured worker's first instinct is often confusion about who's responsible. California generally routes these injuries through workers' compensation, regardless of fault, which means benefits without having to prove your employer was negligent, but also usually without a separate injury lawsuit against your employer. Where the picture changes is when someone outside your employment relationship contributed to the harm: a subcontractor on a shared jobsite, a property owner along Rt 49, or a manufacturer of defective equipment. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we simply connect you with an independent attorney who can review whether your Loyalton workplace injury involves both a comp claim and a third-party case worth pursuing.

whyChoose.title: Why Loyalton Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Untangle Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can open a separate claim. An attorney in our network can sort out which path, or both, applies to your Loyalton injury.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your case, so getting connected with an attorney quickly matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: If you're worried about reporting an injury because of how your employer might react, know that retaliation for filing a workplace injury claim is illegal in California. An independent attorney can advise you on protecting your job while pursuing your claim.

items.question: I work for a small operation near Church Street — does workers' comp still apply?
items.answer: Most California employers, regardless of size, are required to carry workers' compensation coverage. If you're unsure about your specific situation, an independent attorney connected through LawProactive can review the details with you at no cost.

items.question: What if my injury happened because of equipment from an outside supplier?
items.answer: That's exactly the kind of scenario where a third-party claim might exist alongside your workers' comp benefits. Since workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, a claim against an outside supplier or manufacturer follows separate rules, including the general 2-year deadline for injury claims. An attorney can evaluate whether this applies to you.

items.question: How quickly do I need to act after a workplace injury in Loyalton?
items.answer: You should generally notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to protect your workers' comp rights. If a third party may be involved, California's standard 2-year deadline for injury claims typically applies, so it's wise not to wait to get information.
